user_input: I cracked a 9.2 CGPA this semester and everyone's congratulating me, but I spent the last three hours staring at my DSA lab assignment feeling absolutely hollow inside. My parents are already talking about 30 LPA packages and comparing me to my cousin, but I don't even know why I'm coding anymore. It feels like I'm running this endless sprint on a treadmill that's going nowhere, and if I stop, I'll just fall off and break.

My LinkedIn feed is literally just 'I am thrilled to announce...' over and over again while I sit here with three active backlogs and zero interview calls. Everyone seems to have their entire career path mapped out while I'm struggling to just get out of bed and attend a single 9 AM lecture. I feel like an absolute ghost walking through this campus, completely invisible and totally lost about what I'm even doing here.

I forced myself into CSE because everyone said it's the only way to get a secure future, but I hate every single line of code I write. Now I'm sitting in this database management class feeling this deep, terrifying panic that I've trapped myself in a life I don't want. I'm too far in to change my branch, and I honestly don't even know who I am outside of trying to survive these exams.

I turned twenty last week and it just hit me like a train that I'm supposed to be an adult soon. I don't feel like an adult, I feel like a kid pretending to understand how taxes, career roadmaps, and rent work. I look at my friends talking about renting apartments in Bangalore and I just want to lock myself in my room and sleep for a year because the future looks like a massive, dark void.

Now that the chaos of midterms is over and I'm on semester break, the silence is actually worse than the stress. When I was studying, I at least had a distraction, but now I'm just sitting here in my room staring at the ceiling feeling completely numb and purposeless. It's like my entire identity was built on chasing deadlines, and without them, I don't even know what I actually like or who I am.

Everyone is grinding LeetCode, updating their LinkedIn with 'I am thrilled to announce...', and talking about 30 LPA packages. I got an 8.9 CGPA in my fifth semester, but honestly? I feel completely dead inside. I sit in my room staring at these tree and graph algorithms and just think... is this it? Is my whole life just going to be optimization problems for some tech giant? I don't even know what I like anymore, I've spent so long doing what I'm 'supposed' to do.

I cleared all my backlogs this semester and thought I'd feel this massive wave of relief, but I just feel... empty. I looked at the syllabus for the next sem and my mind went blank. My parents are already asking about what kind of roles I'm targeting in campus placements. I lied and said software engineering, but the truth is I don't know who I am anymore outside of just trying not to fail.

I skipped the DSA coding lab today because I just couldn't force myself to get out of bed. My roommate is already on their second internship and my dad keeps forwarding articles about 'recession proof careers' on WhatsApp. I feel like this massive disappointment waiting to happen. I used to love painting and writing, but now my days are just spent doomscrolling and feeling this heavy, suffocating fog about where my life is actually going.

Turning twenty next week and I feel like an absolute fraud. My friends are planning these big birthday parties and talking about their five-year plans, and I'm just sitting here trying not to cry because I changed my major twice and still hate it. I feel like I'm moving backward while everyone else got some secret manual on how to grow up. What if I never find a path that actually feels right?

We had our first placement briefing today and they showed us the package stats and the company logos. Instead of feeling motivated, I felt this sick, hollow dread in my stomach. I've spent four years pulling all-nighters, sacrificing my sleep, and stressing over CGPA just to end up in some corporate cubicle doing work I don't care about? I feel so incredibly lost, like I've built my entire identity on a lie.

I cleared the DSA coding test and actually cracked the tech interview today, but instead of feeling happy, I just went to the washroom and cried. Everyone in the hostel is celebrating their 15 LPA packages and here I am, looking at my offer letter, feeling absolutely nothing. I don't even like coding; I just did it because of the placement stats and my dad's constant comparison with our neighbor's son. Now that I have it, I feel completely empty and lost, like I've walked down a road that leads nowhere.

My parents kept pushing me to take CS because of 'future security', but now I'm in my third year with a 6.2 CGPA, two active backlogs, and absolutely zero interest in what's happening in classes. Every morning I wake up to the sound of alarms and just stare at the ceiling, wondering what the hell I'm even doing here. I used to love sketch art in school, but now I don't even know who I am anymore; I'm just a walking disappointment waiting to get filtered out of the placement drive.

I look at my LinkedIn feed and everyone is either posting about their summer internships at FAANG or sharing certification badges. I spent my entire semester break trying to learn web development, but every time I open VS Code, I just freeze. I feel so incredibly left behind and lost, like everyone has a secret roadmap for life and I missed the orientation session.

Tomorrow is the branch change deadline and my hands are literally shaking while looking at the portal. If I stay in Mechanical, I feel like I'll starve because there are no core jobs, but if I change to IT, I know I'll hate every single coding lab just like I did in my first year. I feel completely trapped in this system where one wrong click at 19 is going to dictate the next 40 years of my life.

It feels like I've just been blindly jumping through hoops my entire life, and now that the hoops are running out, I have no idea who I am without them.
